tagline: Little machines that tell time worse than your phone, and why people pay a fortune for them.
why: Fine watches are one of the few accessories people wear as a quiet signal: of taste, success, or nerdy appreciation for tiny engineering. A mechanical watch is a few hundred hand-finished parts with no battery. Watch talk is really about history, craftsmanship, design icons and the hype around models you can't simply walk in and buy. Hong Kong is one of the world's biggest watch markets, so it comes up constantly.

essentials.title: Mechanical vs quartz
essentials.body: Quartz watches run on a battery and are more accurate. Mechanical watches run on a wound spring, and enthusiasts love them precisely because they're old-school craftsmanship.

essentials.title: The movement is the engine
essentials.body: The movement (or calibre) is the mechanism inside. 'In-house' means the brand makes its own, which carries prestige. Many good brands use reliable movements from suppliers like ETA or Sellita.

essentials.title: Complications are extra functions
essentials.body: Anything beyond hours, minutes and seconds: date, chronograph (stopwatch), GMT (second time zone), moon phase, perpetual calendar, tourbillon, minute repeater. More complications, more cost.

essentials.title: The holy trinity
essentials.body: Patek Philippe, Audemars Piguet and Vacheron Constantin are seen as the top tier of traditional Swiss watchmaking.

essentials.title: Steel sports watches are the hype
essentials.body: Rolex Submariner, GMT-Master II and Daytona, AP Royal Oak, Patek Nautilus. Demand outstrips supply, so there are waitlists, purchase histories and resale prices above retail.

essentials.title: Watch categories
essentials.body: Dive watches, pilot watches, chronographs, dress watches, GMTs and 'integrated bracelet' sports watches. Knowing the category helps you compliment someone's choice.

essentials.title: Price tiers
essentials.body: Roughly: Seiko, Tissot, Hamilton under HK$10,000; Tudor, Longines, Oris and Omega in the tens of thousands; Rolex upward; the trinity and independents into the hundreds of thousands and beyond.

jargon.meaning: A mechanical watch that winds itself from the motion of your wrist.
A mechanical watch you wind by turning the crown.
A built-in stopwatch, usually with pushers beside the crown.
A watch that shows a second time zone, loved by travellers and pilots.
A rotating cage that counters gravity's effect on accuracy. Mostly a show of skill, and very expensive.
The ring around the glass. On dive watches it rotates to time a dive.
The watch face. Special dial colours can double a watch's value.
The knob used to set and wind. Also Rolex's logo.
The glow-in-the-dark paint on hands and markers.
The scratch-resistant glass on good watches.
The brand designs and makes its own movement.
Someone's dream watch, the one they'd buy if money were no object.
A watch sold with its original box and papers, which raises resale value.
Unofficial dealers selling new or nearly new watches, often above retail for hyped models.
A watch built for a job, like diving or flying, rather than dress.
A photo of a watch on someone's wrist. The currency of watch Instagram.
Nicknames for Rolex colourways: red-blue GMT, black-blue GMT, green Submariner.

names.name: Rolex
names.what: The most recognised luxury watch brand. Submariner, Daytona, GMT-Master II and Datejust are its icons.

names.name: Omega
names.what: The Speedmaster was the first watch on the Moon (1969). Also James Bond's watch since 1995 and the Olympics timekeeper.

names.name: Patek Philippe
names.what: Often called the finest watchmaker. Famous for 'You never actually own a Patek Philippe. You merely look after it for the next generation.'

names.name: Audemars Piguet
names.what: Makers of the Royal Oak (1972), the octagonal steel watch that created the luxury sports watch.

names.name: Vacheron Constantin
names.what: Founded 1755, the oldest continuously operating watchmaker. The Overseas is its sports model.

names.name: Gérald Genta
names.what: Designer of the Royal Oak and Patek Nautilus. The most influential watch designer ever.

names.name: Cartier
names.what: Jeweller whose Tank and Santos are timeless dress watches, hugely popular again with younger buyers.

names.name: Grand Seiko
names.what: Japan's high-end brand, admired for incredible finishing and the smooth 'Spring Drive' sweep.

names.name: Seiko
names.what: Japanese giant that launched the first quartz watch; its affordable divers are enthusiast favourites.

names.name: Swatch Group
names.what: Owns Omega, Longines, Tissot, Blancpain, Breguet and Swatch. Its 2022 Omega MoonSwatch caused queues around the block.

names.name: Tudor
names.what: Rolex's sister brand. Similar tool-watch DNA at a friendlier price; the Black Bay is its hit.

names.name: Richard Mille
names.what: Ultra-light, ultra-expensive watches worn by athletes like Rafael Nadal and many Hong Kong tycoons.

names.name: F.P. Journe
names.what: Independent Paris-based watchmaker, a connoisseur favourite whose prices have soared.

names.name: A. Lange & Söhne
names.what: German maker some rank alongside the holy trinity for finishing.

names.name: Hodinkee
names.what: The best-known watch website and media brand.

timeline.event: Vacheron Constantin is founded in Geneva.
Cartier makes the Santos for aviator Alberto Santos-Dumont, an early men's wristwatch.
Rolex launches the Oyster, the first truly waterproof wristwatch.
The Rolex Submariner and Blancpain Fifty Fathoms define the dive watch.
Omega Speedmaster goes to the Moon; Seiko sells the first quartz wristwatch.
The quartz crisis: cheap accurate watches nearly kill Swiss watchmaking.
AP Royal Oak launches, a steel watch priced like gold.
Swatch launches and helps rescue the Swiss industry.
Apple Watch arrives; mechanical watches survive by becoming luxury objects.
Paul Newman's own Rolex Daytona sells for $17.8 million.
Patek discontinues the steel Nautilus 5711, and its resale price spikes.
Resale prices peak, then cool. The MoonSwatch craze peaks too.
Rolex buys Bucherer, the world's biggest watch retailer.

now.headline: The resale bubble cooled
now.detail: Hyped models that traded far above retail in 2022 have come back down, so 'investment watch' talk is quieter.

now.headline: Tariffs and price rises
now.detail: US tariffs on Swiss imports in 2025, plus record gold prices, pushed retail prices up across the industry.

now.headline: Smaller is cool again
now.detail: Many buyers now prefer vintage-style 36 to 39mm cases over the huge watches of the 2000s.

now.headline: Independents are hot
now.detail: Small makers like F.P. Journe, Akrivia and Kari Voutilainen are the new connoisseur favourites.

now.headline: Certified pre-owned
now.detail: Rolex runs its own pre-owned programme through dealers, which is changing the second-hand market.

now.headline: Swiss exports to China slumped
now.detail: Weak demand in mainland China and Hong Kong has hurt Swiss brands since 2024.

local.headline: A watch capital
local.detail: Hong Kong has been one of the world's top markets for Swiss watches for decades. Canton Road, Causeway Bay and Central are lined with boutiques.

local.headline: Grey dealers everywhere
local.detail: Shops in Tsim Sha Tsui and Mong Kok sell hyped models above retail, and many collectors buy and sell through them.

local.headline: Mainland tourists drove the boom
local.detail: Watch shops relied on mainland shoppers; their changing spending habits are a big reason some stores closed.

local.headline: Watch meetups
local.detail: Collector groups meet for 'RedBar'-style evenings and swap wrist shots. It's a sociable hobby.

local.headline: Auctions
local.detail: Christie's, Sotheby's and Phillips hold major watch auctions in Hong Kong.

debates.question: Is a Rolex worth it?
debates.sides: Fans cite build quality and resale value; critics say you pay mostly for the crown logo.

debates.question: Mechanical vs quartz
debates.sides: Quartz is more accurate and cheaper; mechanical fans say a watch should have a soul.

debates.question: Smartwatch or real watch?
debates.sides: Plenty of people wear an Apple Watch for workouts and a mechanical for everything else.

debates.question: Are watches an investment?
debates.sides: A few models have soared, but most watches lose value. Buy what you love.

debates.question: Is the purchase-history game fair?
debates.sides: Buyers complain they must buy other items to get hyped models; brands say they reward loyal customers.

starters: That's a great watch. What is it?
Do you have a grail watch?
Are you a mechanical person or a smartwatch person?
Which do you think is the best design ever made?
Did you get that from an AD or the grey market?
Do you rotate watches or wear one every day?

sayThis.why: Shows you know the difference without sounding like an expert.

sayThis.say: Gérald Genta designed half the icons, right? Royal Oak and Nautilus.
sayThis.why: Enthusiasts love when someone knows the designer.

sayThis.say: I like that it's a sensible size.
sayThis.why: Smaller cases are in fashion, so it's a safe compliment.

sayThis.say: The finishing on Grand Seiko dials is crazy for the price.

sayThis.why: Nicknames show you're in on the culture.

avoid: Asking how much someone's watch cost.
Picking up or touching someone's watch without asking.

quiz.explain: Quartz watches use a battery and a vibrating crystal.

options: Any function beyond telling the time
quiz.explain: Date, chronograph, GMT and moon phase are complications.

quiz.q: Which watch went to the Moon in 1969?
Who designed the AP Royal Oak?
quiz.explain: Genta also designed the Patek Nautilus.

quiz.q: Which three make up the 'holy trinity'?
options: Patek Philippe, Audemars Piguet, Vacheron Constantin
quiz.explain: The traditional top tier of Swiss watchmaking.

quiz.q: What does a GMT watch show?

options: Cheap quartz watches nearly wiping out Swiss makers
quiz.explain: In the 1970s and 80s, mostly from Japanese quartz watches.

A red and blue GMT-Master II
quiz.explain: Named for the red and blue bezel.

quiz.q: What is Tudor's relationship to Rolex?
quiz.explain: Founded by Rolex's founder Hans Wilsdorf.

deep.title: Brand by brand
deep.intro: The models people actually name-drop, and the records that make headlines. Auction prices are hammer prices including fees.

groups.name: Rolex
groups.intro: The world's best-known luxury watch: Swiss, independent (owned by a foundation), and so in demand that steel sports models have waitlists. Fans talk in reference numbers and nicknames.

items.name: Submariner
items.what: The 1953 dive watch: black dial, rotating bezel, Mercedes hands. The no-date ref. 124060 is the purist's pick; the green-bezel 'Kermit' and 'Hulk' are fan favourites.
items.value: The most copied watch in the world

items.name: Cosmograph Daytona
items.what: Racing chronograph with three sub-dials and a tachymeter bezel. Vintage ones with 'exotic' Paul Newman dials are the holy grail.
items.value: Record: Paul Newman's own Daytona, US$17.8m (Phillips, 2017)

items.name: GMT-Master II
items.what: Pilot's watch with a second time zone. Nicknames by bezel: 'Pepsi' (red/blue), 'Batman' (blue/black), 'Root Beer' (brown), 'Sprite' (green/black, left-handed).
items.value: Pepsi on Jubilee bracelet trades well above retail

items.name: Datejust
items.what: The classic everyday Rolex since 1945: date under a 'Cyclops' magnifier, fluted bezel, Jubilee bracelet. Huge choice of dials.

items.name: Day-Date 'President'
items.what: Only in gold or platinum, with the day spelled out at 12. The power watch of presidents and tycoons; the ice-blue dial is reserved for platinum.
items.value: Platinum ice-blue: the ultimate 'I've made it' Rolex

items.name: Explorer and Explorer II
items.what: Tool watches linked to the 1953 Everest climb. Explorer: simple 3-6-9 dial. Explorer II: orange 24-hour hand, the white 'Polar' dial is a cult pick.

items.name: Sea-Dweller and Deepsea
items.what: Heavier dive watches with a helium valve, rated to 1,220 m and 3,900 m. The 'D-Blue' Deepsea marks James Cameron's dive to the Mariana Trench.

items.name: Oyster Perpetual 'Tiffany'
items.what: The simplest Rolex. The 2020 turquoise-dial OP 41 became so hyped that it traded at several times retail.

items.name: Bao Dai (ref. 6062)
items.what: A unique gold moonphase with a black diamond dial, once owned by Vietnam's last emperor.

groups.name: Patek Philippe
groups.intro: Geneva, family-owned since 1932, widely seen as the top of the watch world. Slogan: 'You never actually own a Patek Philippe. You merely look after it for the next generation.'

items.name: Nautilus 5711
items.what: Gérald Genta's 1976 porthole-shaped steel sports watch with a horizontally-embossed blue dial. Patek discontinued it in 2021 and prices exploded.

items.name: Aquanaut
items.what: The Nautilus's younger, sportier sibling with a rubber 'tropical' strap. Popular in Hong Kong as a weekend watch.

items.name: Calatrava
items.what: The definitive round, plain dress watch since 1932. The 'Clous de Paris' hobnail bezel is the classic look.

items.name: Grandmaster Chime 6300A
items.what: Patek's most complicated wristwatch, reversible with two dials and 20 complications. A one-off steel version was made for charity.

items.name: Henry Graves Supercomplication
items.what: A gold pocket watch from 1933 with 24 complications, made for a New York banker. The most famous watch in collecting.

items.name: Perpetual calendar chronographs (ref. 2499, 5270)
items.what: The 'grand complication' every serious collector wants: shows day, date, month, leap year and moon phase, plus a stopwatch.

groups.name: Audemars Piguet
groups.intro: Le Brassus, Switzerland, still family-controlled. Basically defined by one watch, the Royal Oak, and famous for celebrity and athlete fans.

items.name: Royal Oak 'Jumbo' (ref. 15202 / 16202)
items.what: The 1972 original: octagonal bezel with eight hexagonal screws, integrated bracelet, 'Petite Tapisserie' grid dial. Designed by Gérald Genta in one night.
items.value: The watch that invented luxury steel

items.name: Royal Oak Offshore
items.what: The chunky 1993 version nicknamed 'The Beast'. Arnold Schwarzenegger, LeBron James and Jay-Z wore them.

items.name: Royal Oak Perpetual Calendar
items.what: The RO with a full calendar and moonphase; often in black ceramic.

items.name: Code 11.59
items.what: AP's 2019 attempt at a round, modern watch. Mocked at launch, slowly winning fans.

groups.name: Omega
groups.intro: Swatch Group's prestige brand. Big in sports timing (Olympic timekeeper) and space, with real history at friendlier prices than Rolex.

items.name: Speedmaster Professional 'Moonwatch'
items.what: The chronograph NASA qualified in 1965 and the first watch on the Moon in 1969. Hand-wound, black dial, hesalite crystal for purists.

items.name: Seamaster Diver 300M
items.what: James Bond's watch since GoldenEye (1995), with a wave-pattern dial.

items.name: Seamaster Aqua Terra
items.what: The everyday Omega with a teak-pattern dial; office-friendly.

items.name: Constellation
items.what: The 'claws' on the bezel are its signature; a 1980s icon now back in fashion.

items.name: MoonSwatch
items.what: The 2022 bioceramic Speedmaster copies made with Swatch, about HK$2,000. People queued overnight, including in Hong Kong.

groups.name: Cartier
groups.intro: Paris jeweller turned watchmaker. Shape watches (square, rectangle, oval) that fashion people love; vintage Cartier is hot right now.

items.name: Tank
items.what: Inspired by First World War tanks seen from above, launched 1917. Worn by Diana, Jackie Kennedy, Warhol and Timothée Chalamet. Tank Louis Cartier is the classic.

items.name: Santos
items.what: One of the first men's wristwatches (1904), made so aviator Alberto Santos-Dumont could read the time while flying. Square, with screws on the bezel.

items.name: Crash
items.what: A melted-looking watch inspired by a car-crash-damaged Tank (or Dalí, depending who tells it). Tiny production, huge auction prices.
items.value: Vintage Crash London: well over US$1m at auction

items.name: Panthère
items.what: Slim square watch with a bracelet like silk; the 1980s fashion icon, relaunched 2017.

items.name: Ballon Bleu
items.what: Round watch with the crown guarded by a blue sapphire cabochon; very popular first luxury watch.

groups.name: Richard Mille
groups.intro: Founded 2001, made 'the racing machine on the wrist': skeletonised, tonneau-shaped, ultra-light, very expensive (often HK$1-20m). Worn by Nadal, Leclerc, Jackie Chan.

items.name: RM 011
items.what: The skeleton chronograph that made the brand famous, often in carbon composite.

items.name: RM 27 (Rafael Nadal)
items.what: Nadal played Grand Slam finals wearing this; some weigh under 20 g.

items.name: RM 56-02 Sapphire
items.what: Case cut from solid sapphire crystal: fully see-through.

groups.name: Vacheron Constantin
groups.intro: The oldest watchmaker in continuous production (1755). Part of the 'Holy Trinity' with Patek and AP.

items.name: Overseas
items.what: Its luxury sports watch with a Maltese-cross bezel and swappable straps.

items.name: Patrimony
items.what: Minimalist round dress watch.

items.name: Berkley Grand Complication
items.what: Pocket watch with 63 complications unveiled in 2024, the most complicated watch ever made.

groups.name: A. Lange & Söhne and the independents
groups.intro: German high watchmaking from Glashütte, and the independent makers collectors chase.

items.name: Lange 1
items.what: Off-centre dial with a big 'outsize' date; Lange's signature since 1994.

items.name: Datograph
items.what: Lange's chronograph, regarded by many as the most beautiful movement made.

items.name: F.P. Journe Chronomètre à Résonance
items.what: François-Paul Journe's two-balance watch; independent watchmaking's star brand.
items.value: Journe FFC (made with Francis Ford Coppola): US$10.8m (Phillips, 2024)

items.name: Grand Seiko 'Snowflake' (SBGA211)
items.what: Japanese finishing at a fraction of Swiss prices; textured white dial and gliding Spring Drive hand.

items.name: Tudor Black Bay
items.what: Rolex's sister brand; vintage-style diver and the most common 'smart money' first luxury watch.
